debug_refreshing.location: Workbench → Status bar: progress message shown right after View → Toggle IntelliSense Debug opens the IntelliSense Debug panel, while its diagnostics snapshot is being rebuilt.

debug_shown.location: Workbench → Status bar: confirmation shown when the IntelliSense Debug panel reports it became visible through its own controls (not through the View menu toggle).

debug_visibility_hidden.location: Workbench → IntelliSense debug panel → visibility event: status shown when the panel reports that it was hidden.

error.location: Workbench → Status bar → Validate SQL: error message shown when the server-side validation of the editor's SQL fails to run; {error} is the underlying error text from the engine or connection.

fk_status_label.location: Workbench → Status bar → Value completion lookup: label inserted into the lookup progress and result messages for a foreign-key column; {column} is the id column, {table}.{display_column} the referenced table and readable column whose names are listed.

inserted_distinct_plural.location: Workbench → Status bar → Editor “Insert distinct values as IN list” action: success message after the column's distinct values were inserted at the cursor as a comma-separated list; {count} (not 1) is the number of values, {column} the column name.

inserted_distinct_singular.location: Workbench → Status bar → Editor “Insert distinct values as IN list” action: success message when exactly one distinct value was inserted at the cursor; {count} is 1, {column} the column name.

log_validating.location: Log console → validation category: verbose log line written when SQL validation starts for the active tab; {count} is the length of the SQL text in characters.

lookup_distinct_progress.location: Workbench → Status bar → Editor “Insert distinct values as IN list” action: busy message shown while the distinct values of the column under the cursor are queried from the server; {column} is the column name.

lookup_error.location: Query editor → “Insert distinct values as IN list” action: error text that is inserted into the editor in place of the values list when the distinct-values query fails; {error} is the database or connection error.

lookup_progress.location: Workbench → Status bar → Value completion lookup: busy message shown while the editor's value-completion popup fetches column values from the server; {label} is the column name, or the foreign-key description with its referenced table.

no_values_found.location: Workbench → Status bar → Value completion lookup: message shown when the value-completion fetch returned no rows for the column, so the popup has nothing to offer; {column} is the column name.

nothing_to_validate.location: Workbench → Status bar → Validate SQL: message shown when Validate SQL is run on a query tab whose editor is empty or only whitespace.

sending_feedback.location: Workbench → Status bar: busy message shown after the Improve IntelliSense feedback dialog is submitted, while the report is saved and uploaded to SQLLY in the background.

summary.location: Workbench → Status bar → Validate SQL: message shown after validation finishes and problems are underlined in the editor; {summary} is a short tally of the errors and warnings found.

table_column_unresolved.value: 값 조회를 위한 테이블/열을 확인할 수 없습니다
table_column_unresolved.location: Workbench → Status bar → Value completion lookup: error shown when the editor asks for column value suggestions but SQLLY cannot work out which table and column the cursor refers to.

table_reference_unresolved.value: 값 조회를 위한 테이블 참조를 확인할 수 없습니다
table_reference_unresolved.location: Workbench → Status bar → Editor “Insert distinct values as IN list” action: error shown when no table reference (such as a FROM clause) can be found in the SQL to look the column's values up in.

validating.location: Workbench → Status bar → Validate SQL: busy message shown while the editor's SQL is sent to the connected database for validation and the result is pending.

values_found.location: Workbench → Status bar → Value completion lookup: success message after the editor's value-completion popup was filled from the server; {count} is the number of values fetched, {label} the column (or foreign-key) description.

read_failed.location: Main window → Status bar → Saved local data files: error when a saved settings file (saved charts, filters, column layouts, import profiles, deploy carts, scheduled dumps) exists but cannot be read from disk; {path} is the file path and {detail} the operating-system error. Often shown at the start of a longer error, so it has no trailing period.

invalid_json.value: {path} 파일의 형식이 잘못되었습니다({detail}). 내용은 변경하지 않고 그대로 두었습니다.
invalid_json.location: Main window → Status bar → Saved local data files: error when a saved settings file (saved charts, filters, column layouts, import profiles, deploy carts, scheduled dumps) exists but its JSON cannot be parsed, so SQLLY leaves the file unchanged; {path} is the file path and {detail} the parser error. Often shown at the start of a longer error, so it has no trailing period.

connections_unreadable.value: 저장된 연결을 불러올 수 없어 파일을 고치기 전까지는 연결 변경 사항이 저장되지 않습니다: {error}
connections_unreadable.location: Main window → Startup warning toast: shown once at launch when the saved connections file exists but could not be read or parsed; the app shows no saved connections and does not save connection changes, so the file is left untouched for the user to fix or restore; {error} is the technical reason. Full sentence.

session_preserved.value: 마지막 세션을 복원하지 못했습니다. 파일은 {path}에 그대로 보관되어 저장하지 않은 쿼리 텍스트가 사라지지 않았습니다.
session_preserved.location: Main window → Startup warning toast: shown once at launch when the saved workspace session (open tabs and unsaved query text) could not be read; the unreadable file was moved aside instead of being overwritten, and {path} is where it now is, so unsaved scripts can be recovered by hand. Full sentence.

add_server.location: Workbench → Sidebar → Explorer tab → Empty state: clickable accent link under the server icon, shown when no connections are saved yet, that opens the dialog to add a new server connection.

browser_demo.value: 탭 안 데모 — 샘플 데이터베이스만 제공됩니다.
browser_demo.location: Workbench → Sidebar → Explorer tab → Empty state (browser edition only): dim caption under the server icon shown in the web demo when no connections exist; adding servers is not available there.

add_server_button.location: Workbench → Sidebar → Object Explorer toolbar: plus-icon button that opens the new-server connection dialog.

close_filter_tooltip.location: Workbench → Sidebar → Explorer tab → Filter bar: tooltip on the X icon beside the object filter field; clicking it closes the filter field and returns the action bar.

filter_button.location: Workbench → Sidebar → Object Explorer toolbar: search-icon button that opens the object filter field.

filter_placeholder.location: Workbench → Sidebar → Explorer tab → Filter bar: placeholder in the field that filters the object tree by name; text wrapped in slashes such as /pattern/ is matched as a regular expression.

invalid_regex_hint.value: 정규식: /로 패턴을 닫으세요(대소문자 구분은 c 추가)
invalid_regex_hint.location: Workbench → Sidebar → Explorer tab → Filter bar: dim hint under the filter field shown when the text starts with / but the regular expression is not closed, or has a flag other than c (case-sensitive).

regex_badge.location: Workbench → Sidebar → Explorer tab → Filter bar: small dim lowercase tag at the end of the filter row, shown while the filter text is a valid /regex/ pattern to signal regex matching is on.

all.location: Workbench → Sidebar → Explorer options menu → Group by: checkable menu item that shows all servers in one flat list without grouping headings.

by_client.location: Workbench → Sidebar → Explorer options menu → Group by: checkable menu item that groups the Explorer's servers under headings for the client each connection is assigned to.

by_environment.location: Workbench → Sidebar → Explorer options menu → Group by: checkable menu item that groups the Explorer's servers by environment (Local, Dev, Test, Staging, Production).

by_project.location: Workbench → Sidebar → Explorer options menu → Group by: checkable menu item that groups the Explorer's servers under headings for the project each connection belongs to.

by_server.location: Workbench → Sidebar → Explorer options menu → Group by: checkable menu item that groups connections under their server (host) name.

explorer_options_tooltip.location: Workbench → Sidebar → Explorer tab header: tooltip on the vertical three-dot icon at the right of the Explorer/Library tabs that opens the Explorer options menu (grouping, manage connections, collapse, refresh).

library_options_tooltip.location: Workbench → Sidebar → Library tab header: tooltip on the vertical three-dot icon at the right of the Explorer/Library tabs, shown while Library is selected, that opens the Library options menu.

filter_button.location: Workbench → Sidebar → Library tab → Action bar: small button with a search icon that opens a filter field for narrowing the saved query library by name.

new_folder_button.location: Workbench → Sidebar → Library tab → Action bar: small button with a plus icon that starts creating a new folder in the saved query library.

save_query_button.location: Workbench → Sidebar → Library tab → Action bar: small button with a save icon that saves the active query tab into the SQL library.

collapse_all.location: Workbench → Sidebar → Explorer options menu: menu item that collapses every expanded node in the Explorer object tree.

group_by.location: Workbench → Sidebar → Explorer options menu: non-clickable section heading at the top, above the grouping choices (All, By client, By project, etc.).

manage_connections.location: Workbench → Sidebar → Explorer options menu: menu item below the grouping choices that opens the connection manager to edit, add, or delete saved connections.

refresh.location: Workbench → Sidebar → Explorer options menu: last menu item, which reloads the schema (databases, tables, and other objects) shown in the Explorer tree.

explorer.location: Workbench → Sidebar → Panel tabs: first tab at the top of the sidebar that shows the Explorer, the tree of connected servers and their database objects.

library.location: Workbench → Sidebar → Panel tabs: second tab at the top of the sidebar that shows the Library of saved SQL queries and folders.

account_signed_in_tooltip.location: Workbench → Status bar → Left icon cluster: tooltip on the account icon while the user is signed in to their SQLLY account (the icon turns green); clicking opens the account details.

account_tooltip.location: Workbench → Status bar → Left icon cluster: tooltip on the first, person-shaped icon when not signed in; clicking it opens the account / sign-in surface.

diagnostics_tooltip.location: Workbench → Status bar → Left icon cluster: tooltip on the fourth icon, which toggles the diagnostics log console and can carry a red badge with the error count.

security_tooltip.location: Workbench → Status bar → Left icon cluster: tooltip on the third, shield icon that opens the security settings surface.

settings_tooltip.location: Workbench → Status bar → Left icon cluster: tooltip on the second, gear icon that opens the Settings window.

label.location: Workbench → Status bar → Right cluster: short text label next to the command icon; clicking it opens the Command Palette.

tooltip.location: Workbench → Status bar → Right cluster: tooltip on the Commands button that names the Command Palette and its keyboard shortcut (⌘K).

disconnected.location: Tab switcher → Tab rows: dim text in a tab's connection trail (where client, project, environment, server, and database normally appear) when that tab has no active connection.

not_connected.location: Workbench → Status bar → Left cluster: connection label shown in place of the server name when no connection is active or the active connection is unhealthy.

dev.location: Connection environment names → Dev (development): shown as the environment badge in the status bar, on Welcome-screen connection cards, and in connection details such as the delete-connection and query-resume dialogs.

local.location: Connection environment names → Local (a database on this machine): shown on Welcome-screen connection cards and in connection details such as the delete-connection and query-resume dialogs; no status-bar badge.

production.location: Connection environment names → Production (live system): shown as the environment badge in the status bar, on Welcome-screen connection cards, and in delete-connection and query-resume dialogs.

staging.location: Connection environment names → Staging (pre-release copy): shown as the environment badge in the status bar, on Welcome-screen connection cards, and in delete-connection and query-resume dialogs.

test.location: Connection environment names → Test (testing system): shown as the environment badge in the status bar, on Welcome-screen connection cards, and in delete-connection and query-resume dialogs.

unset.location: Connection environment names → Unset (no environment assigned): appears on Welcome-screen connection cards and in delete-connection and query-resume dialogs; no status-bar badge.

error_plural.location: Workbench → Status bar → Left cluster: dim indicator shown while IntelliSense has hit two or more internal errors for the active tab; {count} is the number of errors.

error_singular.location: Workbench → Status bar → Left cluster: dim indicator shown when IntelliSense has hit exactly one internal error for the active tab; {count} is 1 (singular form).

copy_open_tooltip.location: Workbench → Status bar → Message area: tooltip on a copyable status message (errors and other long messages); clicking copies the full text and opens it in a readable dialog.

locked.location: Workbench → Status bar → Right badges: amber all-caps chip shown while connected to a Production-environment connection whose production safety lock is engaged (write protection on).

unlocked.location: Workbench → status bar → production chip while writes are temporarily unlocked: uppercase environment label followed by the unlock countdown in {remaining}.

locked.location: Workbench → status bar → read-only connection chip while writes are locked: connection mode label.

unlocked.location: Workbench → status bar → read-only connection chip while writes are temporarily unlocked: mode label followed by the unlock countdown in {remaining}.

direct_tooltip.location: Workbench → Status bar: tooltip on the green connection dot when queries go straight from this app to the database; {server} is the server's display name.

not_connected_tooltip.location: Workbench → Status bar: tooltip on the red connection dot shown when there is no active connection, so queries have no route.

relay_tooltip.location: Workbench → Status bar: tooltip on the green connection dot for a remote connection, showing the path queries take; {relay_host} is the relay server, {bridge_name} the bridge device, {server} the database server.

many.location: Workbench → status bar → background-task chip with multiple running tasks: plural task count in {count}.

one.location: Workbench → status bar → background-task chip with exactly one running task: singular task count.

pending.location: Workbench → status bar → manual-commit chip: transaction mode followed by the number of uncommitted statements in {count}.

app_store_tooltip.value: Mac App Store 버전 — 업데이트는 App Store를 통해 제공됩니다
app_store_tooltip.location: Workbench → Status bar → Version label: tooltip in the Mac App Store edition, explaining that SQLLY does not check for updates itself because updates come through the App Store.

available.location: Workbench → status bar → update-available chip: alert naming the newer application version in {version}, prefixed with a lowercase v.

available_tooltip.value: 새 업데이트 있음 — 클릭하면 자세히 보기
available_tooltip.location: Workbench → Status bar → Version label: tooltip shown when a newer version is available; clicking the version opens the update details.

check_tooltip.location: Workbench → Status bar → Version label: tooltip shown when no update is known yet; clicking the version checks for a newer release now.

download_tooltip.location: Workbench → Status bar → Update chip: tooltip on the accent-coloured chip naming the new version; clicking it shows the release notes and download.

tooltip.location: Workbench → Status bar → Right cluster: tooltip on the percentage label (for example 100%) that opens the editor zoom control.

copied_status.location: Workbench → Status bar: success message shown after the Copy button in the status message detail dialog puts the full message on the clipboard.

copy_button.location: Status message detail dialog → Footer buttons (copy): button at the bottom of the dialog (opened by clicking a status-bar message) that copies the full message text to the clipboard.

error_title.location: Status message detail dialog → Title bar (error): dialog title used when the clicked status-bar message is an error; the full red error text is shown below it.

message_title.location: Status message detail dialog → Title bar (message): dialog title used when the clicked status-bar message is informational or a success (neither an error nor a warning).

warning_title.location: Status message detail dialog → Title bar (warning): dialog title used when the clicked status-bar message is a warning; the full warning text is shown below it.

account_fallback.location: SQLLY Store Sign In window → Status line: stand-in inserted into “Signed in as …” when the store account has no email address on record; lowercase, used mid-sentence.

account_row.location: SQLLY Store Sign In window → Signed-in view: first detail line under the heading, naming the store account this app is signed in to; {email} is the account email address.

activate.location: SQLLY Store Sign In window → Pairing view: primary button under the large pairing code; opens the store's device registration page in the web browser so the user can sign in and claim this device.

retry.location: SQLLY Store Sign In window → Failed view: primary button shown when getting a pairing code from the store failed; requests a fresh pairing code.

sign_out_switch.location: SQLLY Store Sign In window → Signed-in view: outline button under the account and device lines that signs out and starts a new pairing so another account can sign in.

device_fallback.location: SQLLY Store Sign In window → Signed-in view: stand-in inserted as the device name in the “Device: …” line when this computer's name cannot be read; lowercase.

device_row.location: SQLLY Store Sign In window → Signed-in view: dim second detail line identifying this computer; {device} is the computer name, {device_id} the store's device identifier.

heading.location: SQLLY Store Sign In window → Body heading: large bold heading at the top of the window body, shown in every state (checking, pairing, signed in, failed).

window_title.location: SQLLY Store Sign In window → Title bar: title shown in the window's title bar (and window menus) for the separate store sign-in window.

no_email.location: SQLLY Store Sign In window → Signed-in view: stand-in shown in parentheses in the “Account: …” line when the signed-in store account has no email address.

paired_fallback.location: SQLLY Store Sign In window → Signed-in view: stand-in placed inside the parentheses of the “Device: …” line when the store returned no device identifier; means the device is paired.

browser_instructions.value: Google, Microsoft, GitHub, Apple, 패스키 또는 이메일로 로그인하기 위해 브라우저를 엽니다. 이 창은 자동으로 완료됩니다.
browser_instructions.location: SQLLY Store Sign In window → Pairing view: small dim explanation under the activate button, telling the user which sign-in options the browser page offers and that this window completes on its own.

code_label.location: SQLLY Store Sign In window → Pairing view: dim label directly above the large pairing code the user confirms on the store's web page; ends with a colon.

awaiting_claim.location: SQLLY Store Sign In window → Status line: progress text shown under the pairing code while the app polls the store, waiting for the user to finish signing in in the browser.

checking_account.location: SQLLY Store Sign In window → Status line: progress text shown immediately when the window opens, while the saved sign-in is read from the keychain.

getting_pairing_code.location: SQLLY Store Sign In window → Pairing progress text: progress text shown in the body and status line while the app requests a pairing code from the store (first open, retry, or after signing out).

keychain_save_failed.location: SQLLY Store Sign In window → Status line: red error shown when the browser sign-in succeeded but the session could not be stored in the OS keychain; {error} is the keychain error.

pairing_task_failed.location: SQLLY Store Sign In window → Status line: red technical error shown when the background task that requests a pairing code crashed or was cancelled; {error} is the internal error text.

poll_task_failed.location: SQLLY Store Sign In window → Status line: red technical error shown when the background task checking for the browser sign-in crashed, which stops the waiting; {error} is the internal error.

signed_in.location: SQLLY Store Sign In window → Status line: confirmation shown when the window opens already signed in or once the browser sign-in completes; {email} is the account email or a stand-in.

waiting_with_error.location: SQLLY Store Sign In window → Status line: progress text shown when one check for the browser sign-in failed temporarily and waiting continues; {error} is the error from that attempt.

connected.location: Workbench → editor tab → accessibility announcement: lowercase state spoken for a tab with an active connection.

deleted_on_disk.location: Workbench → editor tab → accessibility announcement: lowercase state spoken when the tab's backing file was deleted on disk.

disconnected.location: Workbench → editor tab → accessibility announcement: lowercase state spoken for a tab without an active connection.

modified_on_disk.location: Workbench → editor tab → accessibility announcement: lowercase state spoken when the tab's backing file changed on disk.

running.location: Workbench → Query tab strip → Tab tooltip and accessibility text: lowercase state word added to the comma-separated tab status when a query is currently executing in that tab.

selected.location: Workbench → editor tab → accessibility announcement: lowercase state spoken for the currently selected tab.

unsaved.location: Workbench → editor tab → accessibility announcement: lowercase state spoken for a tab with unsaved changes.

connected.location: Workbench → All Tabs menu → clean, connected, idle row: query name and server without additional state text.

connected_running.location: Workbench → All Tabs menu → clean, connected, running row: query name and server followed by the running state.

dirty.location: Workbench → All Tabs menu → dirty, unconnected, idle row: bullet marking unsaved changes before the query name.

dirty_connected.location: Workbench → All Tabs menu → dirty, connected, idle row: bullet marking unsaved changes before the query name and server.

dirty_connected_running.location: Workbench → All Tabs menu → dirty, connected, running row: unsaved-changes bullet, query name, server, and running state.

dirty_running.location: Workbench → All Tabs menu → dirty, unconnected, running row: unsaved-changes bullet and query name followed by the running state.

name_only.location: Workbench → All Tabs menu → clean, unconnected, idle row: just the query tab's name with no state text; {name} is the tab name, so usually leave this as only the placeholder.

running.location: Workbench → All Tabs menu → clean, unconnected, running row: query name followed by the running state.

notebook_prefix.location: Workbench → Notebook tabs: leading word with trailing space of the automatic notebook name, used to recognise auto-named notebook tabs when restoring a session; must match the start of “Notebook {number}”.

notebook_title.location: Workbench → Tab strip: automatic name of a new notebook tab that has no file yet; {number} is the running tab counter (for example “Notebook 3”).

query_prefix.location: Workbench → Query tabs: leading word with trailing space of the automatic query name, used to recognise auto-named tabs and, trimmed, as the fallback name of a file tab; must match the start of “Query {number}”.

query_title.location: Workbench → Tab strip: automatic name given to a new or untitled query tab until it is renamed, saved, or auto-named from its SQL; {number} is the tab number (for example “Query 2”).

cancel_button.location: Close tab → Unsaved changes prompt: third button (Cancel) of the warning shown when closing a query tab with unsaved changes; dismisses the prompt and keeps the tab open.

discard_button.location: Close tab → Unsaved changes prompt: second button of the warning shown when closing a tab with unsaved changes; closes the tab and throws the changes away without saving.

fallback_name.location: Close tab and file-changed-on-disk prompts → Tab name fallback: stand-in inserted where the tab name would appear in the prompt message if the tab's name cannot be found; lowercase, used mid-sentence.

save_button.location: Close tab → Unsaved changes prompt: first, default button of the warning shown when closing a tab with unsaved changes; saves the file (asking for a location if untitled) and then closes the tab.

staged_edits_detail.value: 결과 그리드의 행 변경 내용이 아직 데이터베이스에 저장되지 않았습니다. 결과 도구 모음에서 저장하거나, 변경 내용을 버려야 탭을 닫을 수 있습니다.
staged_edits_detail.location: Close tab → Unsaved grid edits prompt: explanatory detail text under the “has unsaved grid edits” question, shown when closing a query tab whose results hold staged row changes that were never saved to the database.

staged_edits_discard_button.location: Close tab → Unsaved grid edits prompt: first button of the warning shown when closing a tab whose results hold staged row changes; throws the staged changes away and closes the tab (the unsaved-text prompt still follows if the SQL text is unsaved).

staged_edits_message.value: “{name}”에 저장되지 않은 그리드 편집 내용이 있습니다. 버리고 닫으시겠습니까?
staged_edits_message.location: Close tab → Unsaved grid edits prompt: question shown when closing a query tab whose results grid holds staged row changes not yet saved to the database; {name} is the tab name.

unsaved_detail.value: 이 탭을 닫으면 변경한 내용이 모두 사라집니다. 저장을 누르면 먼저 파일에 저장되며, 이 쿼리를 한 번도 저장하지 않았다면 위치를 선택합니다.
unsaved_detail.location: Close tab → Unsaved changes prompt: explanatory detail text under the “has unsaved changes” question, describing what Don't Save discards and what Save does.

unsaved_message.value: “{name}”에 저장되지 않은 변경 사항이 있습니다. 그래도 닫겠습니까?
unsaved_message.location: SQLLY → Workbench → Editor tabs → close: text shown as ““{name}” has unsaved changes. Close it anyway?”.

close_button.location: Tab context menu → Close Others / Close to the Right / Close All → Unsaved tabs prompt: first button, which also closes the tabs with unsaved changes and discards those changes.

keep_button.location: Tab context menu → Close Others / Close to the Right / Close All → Unsaved tabs prompt: cancel button that leaves the tabs with unsaved changes open (clean tabs are already closed).

kept_plural.value: 저장되지 않은 변경 사항이 있는 탭 {count}개를 유지했습니다
kept_plural.location: Workbench → Status bar: message shown when tabs are closed automatically on disconnect but two or more tabs with unsaved changes were left open; {count} is the number of tabs kept.

kept_singular.value: 저장되지 않은 변경 사항이 있는 탭 {count}개를 유지했습니다
kept_singular.location: Workbench → Status bar: message shown when tabs are closed automatically on disconnect but exactly one tab with unsaved changes was left open; {count} is 1 (singular form).

unsaved_detail.value: 닫으면 파일에 저장되지 않은 변경 사항이 사라집니다.
unsaved_detail.location: Tab context menu → Close Others / Close to the Right / Close All → Unsaved tabs prompt: detail text under the question, warning that closing loses changes not saved to a file.

unsaved_plural.value: 탭 {count}개에 저장되지 않은 변경 사항이 있습니다. 이 탭들도 닫으시겠습니까?
unsaved_plural.location: Tab context menu → Close Others / Close to the Right / Close All → Unsaved tabs prompt: question shown after the clean tabs closed when two or more remaining tabs have unsaved changes; {count} is that number.

unsaved_singular.value: 탭 {count}개에 저장되지 않은 변경 사항이 있습니다. 이 탭도 닫으시겠습니까?
unsaved_singular.location: Tab context menu → Close Others / Close to the Right / Close All → Unsaved tabs prompt: question shown when exactly one remaining tab has unsaved changes; {count} is 1 (singular form).

choose_database.location: Workbench → Editor tab strip → Connection chip: lowercase prompt shown in place of the database name when the active tab is connected to a server but no database is selected yet; invites picking one.

not_connected.location: Workbench → Editor tab strip → Connection chip: label shown instead of a server name when the active query tab has no server connection at all.

server_database.location: Workbench → Editor tab strip → Connection chip: compact label for a connected tab; {server} is the connection name and {database} the selected database, separated by a middle dot.

server_disconnected.location: Workbench → Editor tab strip → Connection chip: label shown when the tab remembers a server connection that is currently disconnected; {server} is the saved connection name.

close.location: Workbench → Editor tab strip → Tab right-click menu: menu item that closes the clicked tab (prompting to save if unsaved); disabled while the tab is pinned.

close_all.location: Workbench → Editor tab strip → Tab right-click menu: menu item that closes every open query tab in the window, prompting for any with unsaved changes.

close_others.location: Workbench → Editor tab strip → Tab right-click menu: menu item that closes all tabs except the one that was right-clicked; enabled only when more than one tab is open.

close_right.location: Workbench → Editor tab strip → Tab right-click menu: menu item that closes every tab positioned to the right of the clicked tab; enabled only when such tabs exist.

copy_path.location: Workbench → Editor tab strip → Tab right-click menu: menu item, shown only for tabs saved to a file, that copies the file's full path to the clipboard.

move_new_window.location: Workbench → Editor tab strip → Tab right-click menu: menu item (desktop only) that moves the tab with its text, connection and results into a newly opened workbench window.

path_copied_status.location: Workbench → Status bar: short confirmation shown after choosing Copy path in the tab right-click menu, meaning the tab's file path is now on the clipboard.

pin.location: Workbench → Editor tab strip → Tab right-click menu: first menu item, shown on an unpinned tab, that pins it so it cannot be closed by accident; verb.

recent_files.location: Workbench → Editor tab strip → Tab right-click menu: small dimmed section heading above the list of up to eight recently opened SQL files, which reopen when clicked.

rename.location: Workbench → Editor tab strip → Tab right-click menu: menu item that turns the tab title into an inline text field so the user can type a new tab name; verb.

reveal_file_manager.location: Workbench → Editor tab strip → Tab right-click menu: Windows/Linux menu item, shown for file-backed tabs, that opens the system file manager at the tab's saved file.

reveal_finder.location: Workbench → Editor tab strip → Tab right-click menu: macOS menu item, shown for file-backed tabs, that opens Finder with the tab's saved file selected; keep Apple's “Finder” name.

unpin.location: Workbench → Editor tab strip → Tab right-click menu: first menu item, shown in place of Pin on a pinned tab, that unpins it so it can be closed again; verb.

adopted.location: Workbench → Status bar: success message in the receiving window after a tab is moved into it from another window; {name} is the moved tab's title.

completed.location: Workbench → Status bar: info message in the original window after one of its tabs has been moved out to another workbench window and closed here.

notebook_unsupported.value: 노트북 탭은 아직 다른 창으로 이동할 수 없습니다.
notebook_unsupported.location: Workbench → Status bar: warning shown when the user tries Move to New Window / Move to Window on a notebook tab, which cannot be moved between windows yet.

query_only.value: 쿼리 탭만 다른 창으로 이동할 수 있습니다.
query_only.location: Workbench → Status bar: warning shown when moving a tab to another window is refused because the tab is a DDL view or read-only snapshot rather than a plain query editor.

query_running.value: 탭을 이동하기 전에 쿼리가 끝날 때까지 기다리거나 쿼리를 취소하세요.
query_running.location: Workbench → Status bar: warning shown when the user tries to move a tab to another window while its query is still running; the move is refused.

reading_results.value: 탭을 이동할 준비 중 — 디스크에서 결과를 읽는 중…
reading_results.location: Results → Grid caption: progress text shown while large on-disk results are read into memory just before a tab is moved to another window; ends with an ellipsis.

results_banner.value: 다른 창에서 가져온 결과입니다 — 새로 고치려면 다시 실행하세요
results_banner.location: Results → Banner above the grid: notice on a tab moved in from another window, saying the results shown are a carried-over copy and re-running the query refreshes them.

results_truncated_banner.value: 다른 창에서 가져온 결과입니다 — 큰 결과는 처음 {count}개 행만 표시되며, 새로 고치려면 다시 실행하세요
results_truncated_banner.location: Results → Banner above the grid: variant of the moved-results notice for large result sets that were cut down; {count} is the maximum number of rows carried over per set.

review_pending.value: 탭을 이동하기 전에 보류 중인 변경 내용 검토를 확인하거나 취소하세요.
review_pending.location: Workbench → Status bar: warning shown when a tab cannot move to another window because a change-review (mutation confirmation) dialog is still open for it.

staged_edits.value: 탭을 이동하기 전에 그리드 편집 내용을 저장하거나 버리세요.
staged_edits.location: Workbench → Status bar: warning shown when a tab cannot move to another window because it has unsaved staged edits in the results grid.

tab_missing.location: Workbench → Status bar: warning shown when a tab move is requested for a tab that was closed in the meantime, so there is nothing left to move.

target_missing.value: “{name}” 탭을 이동할 수 없습니다 — 대상 창이 닫혔습니다.
target_missing.location: Workbench → Status bar: error shown when moving a tab fails because the destination window was closed before the move completed; {name} is the tab's title.

transaction_open.value: 탭을 이동하기 전에 열린 트랜잭션을 커밋하거나 롤백하세요.
transaction_open.location: Workbench → Status bar: warning shown when a tab cannot move to another window because it still has an open manual-commit transaction.

window_label.location: Workbench → Editor tab strip → Tab right-click menu: item that moves the tab into another open window; {number} is that window's number; used when the window has no active tab name.

window_with_tab_label.location: Workbench → Editor tab strip → Tab right-click menu: item that moves the tab into another window; {number} is the window number and {tab} that window's active tab name, to tell windows apart.

ai.location: Workbench → Main area region switcher: short name of the AI assistant drawer region, used when cycling or jumping between the editor, history, DDL, plan and AI regions.

ddl.location: Workbench → Main area region switcher: short name of the DDL (object definition script) panel region below the editor; keep the technical abbreviation.

editor.location: Workbench → Main area region switcher: short name of the SQL editor region of the active query tab, the default region.

history.location: Workbench → Main area region switcher: short name of the History panel region that lists previous runs and versions of the active tab's query.

plan.location: Workbench → Main area region switcher: short name of the execution Plan panel region where captured query plans are displayed.

placeholder.location: Workbench → Editor tab strip → Inline rename field: placeholder inside the text field that replaces a tab's title after choosing Rename, before the user types.

none.value: 다시 열 수 있는 닫힌 탭이 없습니다
none.location: Workbench → Status bar: info message shown when Reopen Closed Tab (Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+T) is used but no recently closed tabs remain in this window.

browser_unavailable.location: Browser version → Unsaved tab close prompt: status-bar error shown when the user picks Save while closing a tab in the browser build, where saving files is not possible.

failed.location: Workbench → Status bar: error shown when choosing Save in the close-unsaved-tab prompt fails to write the file; {error} is the operating system's error text. The tab stays open.

feature_unavailable.location: Browser version → Unsaved tab close prompt: description of the missing feature passed into the generic browser “not available” message when saving a tab is attempted in the browser build.

succeeded.location: Workbench → Status bar: success message after choosing Save in the close-unsaved-tab prompt writes the file and closes the tab; {path} is the saved file's full path.

close_label.location: Workbench → Editor tab strip: tooltip and accessible name of the small × close button on each tab; {title} is that tab's title.

tooltip.location: Workbench → Editor tab strip: hover tooltip on a tab; {title} is the tab title and {status} a comma-separated list of states such as selected, unsaved, connected or running.

choose_database_placeholder.location: Workbench → Query toolbar → Database dropdown: lowercase placeholder shown when connected to a server but no database has been chosen yet, prompting a choice.

database_placeholder.location: Workbench → Query toolbar → Database dropdown: placeholder naming the empty picker when no server is connected (the dropdown is then disabled); noun.

database_tooltip.location: Workbench → Query toolbar: tooltip on the database icon beside the Database dropdown, explaining that it selects which database the active tab queries.

edit_disconnected_tooltip.location: Workbench → Query toolbar: tooltip on the dimmed gear (edit connection) button beside the pickers while no server is connected, explaining why it is disabled.

edit_tooltip.location: Workbench → Query toolbar: tooltip on the gear button beside the server/database pickers that opens the connection editor; {name} is the active connection's name.

no_databases.location: Workbench → Query toolbar → Database dropdown: empty-state text in the open list when the connected server reports no databases to choose from.

server_placeholder.location: Workbench → Query toolbar → Server dropdown: placeholder shown in the server connection picker when no saved connection is selected; noun.

server_tooltip.location: Workbench → Query toolbar: tooltip on the server icon beside the Server dropdown, explaining that it picks which saved server connection the tab uses.

toggle_tooltip.location: Workbench → Query toolbar: tooltip on the clock icon button that shows or hides the active tab's version history panel; keep the ⌘⌥H shortcut as is.

capture_tooltip.location: Workbench → Query toolbar: tooltip on the execution-plan icon button that runs the query and captures its actual execution plan; keep the ⌘L shortcut as is.

capture_with_options_tooltip.location: Workbench → Query toolbar: tooltip on the execution-plan button when extra plan options are enabled; {summary} lists the active options (e.g. ANALYZE, BUFFERS).

stacked_tooltip.value: 결과 집합이 쌓여 있습니다 — 클릭하면 결과 집합마다 탭으로 표시됩니다
stacked_tooltip.location: Workbench → Query toolbar: tooltip on the results-layout button while multiple result sets are shown stacked in one panel; clicking switches to one tab per result set.

tabbed_tooltip.value: 결과 집합이 탭으로 표시되어 있습니다 — 클릭하면 쌓아서 표시됩니다
tabbed_tooltip.location: Workbench → Query toolbar: tooltip on the results-layout button while each result set has its own tab; clicking switches to showing them stacked in one panel.

all.location: Workbench → Query toolbar → Run button: internal name of the run-all-statements mode; the visible button text and tooltip come from the matching “Run all” label entries.

all_label.location: Workbench → Query toolbar: text on the accent Run button when the editor holds several statements and no selection; {count} is the number of statements that will run.

all_tooltip.location: Workbench → Query toolbar: tooltip on the Run button in run-all mode; {count} is the number of statements in the tab; keep the F5 / ⌘↩ shortcuts as is.

cancel.location: Workbench → Query toolbar → Run button: internal name of the cancel mode used while a query runs; the visible text comes from the companion Cancel label entry.

cancel_label.location: Workbench → Query toolbar: text on the primary Run button while a query is executing, when the button turns into a Cancel button that stops the query; verb.

cancel_tooltip.location: Workbench → Query toolbar: tooltip on the Run button while it acts as Cancel during query execution; keep the ⌘⎋ (Cmd+Escape) shortcut as is.

default.location: Workbench → Query toolbar → Run button: internal name of the plain run mode (single statement, nothing selected); the visible text comes from the “Run” label entry.

default_label.location: Workbench → Query toolbar: text on the accent primary button that runs the active tab's query (single statement, no selection); short imperative verb.

default_tooltip.location: Workbench → Query toolbar: tooltip on the primary Run button in its default mode, explaining it runs the query; keep the F5 / ⌘↩ shortcuts as is.

file.location: Workbench → Query toolbar → Run button: internal name of the run-whole-file mode for file-backed tabs; the visible text comes from the “Run file” label entry.

file_label.location: Workbench → query toolbar → Run button for a file-backed editor with at most one statement: button label.

file_tooltip.location: Workbench → query toolbar → Run button for a file-backed editor: tooltip explaining that the whole file runs, including keyboard shortcuts.

procedure.location: Workbench → Query toolbar → Run button: internal name of the procedure mode (deploy then run); the visible text comes from the “Run procedure” label entry.

procedure_label.location: Workbench → query toolbar → Run button in procedure mode: button label.

procedure_tooltip.location: Workbench → query toolbar → Run button in procedure mode: tooltip explaining procedure deployment and execution, including keyboard shortcuts.

selection.location: Workbench → Query toolbar → Run button: internal name of the run-selected-text mode; the visible text comes from the “Run selection” label entry.

selection_label.location: Workbench → query toolbar → Run button with selected SQL: button label.

selection_tooltip.location: Workbench → query toolbar → Run button with selected SQL: tooltip explaining that only selected text runs, including keyboard shortcuts.

statement.location: Workbench → Query toolbar → Run button: internal name of the run-statement-under-caret mode; the visible text comes from the “Run statement” label entry.

statement_label.location: Workbench → query toolbar → Run button in current-statement mode: button label.

statement_tooltip.location: Workbench → query toolbar → Run button in current-statement mode: tooltip explaining that the statement under the caret runs, including keyboard shortcuts.

refresh_no_snapshot_tooltip.value: 데이터 모델 새로 고침 — 스냅샷이 아직 로드되지 않음
refresh_no_snapshot_tooltip.location: Workbench → Query toolbar: tooltip on the refresh-schema icon button when no cached data-model snapshot exists yet for the connection; clicking reloads schema metadata.

refresh_with_age_tooltip.location: Workbench → Query toolbar: tooltip on the refresh-schema icon button; {age} is when the cached data model was fetched (date and time plus how long ago).

refreshed_status.location: Workbench → Status bar: success message after clicking the toolbar refresh-schema button, once connections and the server's schema tree and completions are reloaded.

label.location: Workbench → Query toolbar → Query toggles: very short abbreviation (2–4 characters) for the actual execution plan toggle, used where a text label replaces its icon.

tooltip.location: Workbench → Query toolbar → Query toggles: tooltip/name of the toggle that turns on capture of the actual execution plan when the query runs.

label.location: Workbench → Query toolbar → Query toggles: very short abbreviation (2–4 characters) for the AI autocomplete toggle, used where a text label replaces its icon.

tooltip.location: Workbench → Query toolbar → Overflow (⋮) menu: checkable item and tooltip for the per-tab toggle that turns AI inline ghost-text completions on or off.

label.location: Workbench → Query toolbar → Query toggles: very short abbreviation (2–4 characters) for the auto format toggle, used where a text label replaces its icon.

tooltip.location: Workbench → Query toolbar → Overflow (⋮) menu: checkable item and tooltip for the toggle that formats the SQL in the editor automatically right before each run.

label.location: Workbench → Query toolbar → Query toggles: very short abbreviation (2–4 characters) for the estimated execution plan toggle, used where a text label replaces its icon.

tooltip.location: Workbench → Query toolbar → Query toggles: tooltip/name of the toggle that shows the estimated execution plan (without running the query).

procedure_detected_tooltip.value: 프로시저 스크립트가 감지되었습니다. 매개변수를 편집하고 배포 후 실행하려면 켜세요.
procedure_detected_tooltip.location: Workbench → Query toolbar → Query toggles: tooltip on the highlighted Procedure mode toggle when the script starts with CREATE/ALTER PROCEDURE but procedure mode is off.

label.location: Workbench → Query toolbar → Query toggles: very short abbreviation (2–4 characters) for the procedure mode toggle, used where a text label replaces its icon.

tooltip.value: 프로시저 모드: 배포한 후 매개변수와 함께 실행
tooltip.location: Workbench → Query toolbar → Overflow (⋮) menu: checkable item and tooltip for procedure mode, where Run first deploys the procedure script and then calls it with parameters.

label.location: Workbench → Query toolbar → Query toggles: very short abbreviation (2–4 characters) for the query resume toggle, used where a text label replaces its icon.

tooltip.location: Workbench → Query toolbar → Overflow (⋮) menu: checkable item and fallback tooltip for the per-tab Query Resume toggle that saves this tab's query state for restore.

label.location: Workbench → Query toolbar → Query toggles: very short abbreviation (2–4 characters) for the run-current-statement toggle, used where a text label replaces its icon.

tooltip.location: Workbench → Query toolbar → Overflow (⋮) menu: checkable item and tooltip for the toggle that makes Run execute only the statement under the caret when nothing is selected.

label.location: Workbench → Query toolbar → Query toggles: very short abbreviation (2–4 characters) for the include-statistics toggle, used where a text label replaces its icon.

tooltip.location: Workbench → Query toolbar → Overflow (⋮) menu: checkable item and tooltip for the toggle that adds time and I/O statistics to runs (shown in the Messages pane).

label.location: Workbench → Query toolbar → Query toggles: very short abbreviation (2–4 characters) for the track-difference toggle, used where a text label replaces its icon.

tooltip.location: Workbench → Query toolbar → Overflow (⋮) menu: checkable item and tooltip for the toggle that compares each run's results with the previous run and highlights the differences.

auto_tooltip.value: 자동 커밋 — 수동 커밋 모드로 전환하려면 클릭
auto_tooltip.location: Workbench → Query toolbar: tooltip on the “A” transaction-mode badge while the tab is in auto-commit mode; clicking switches the tab to manual commit mode.

commit_label.location: Workbench → Query toolbar: text on the button that appears in manual commit mode while a transaction is open; commits the pending changes; verb.

commit_tooltip.location: Workbench → Query toolbar: tooltip on the Commit button shown in manual commit mode, which commits the tab's open transaction to the database.

lost_tooltip.value: 트랜잭션이 손실되었습니다 — 새 트랜잭션을 시작하려면 다시 실행하세요
lost_tooltip.location: Workbench → Query toolbar: tooltip on the transaction-mode badge when the tab's manual transaction was lost (e.g. the session dropped); running again starts a new one.

manual_tooltip.value: 수동 커밋 모드 — 자동 커밋으로 전환하려면 클릭
manual_tooltip.location: Workbench → Query toolbar: tooltip on the “M” transaction-mode badge while the tab is in manual commit mode; clicking switches back to auto-commit.

rollback_label.location: Workbench → Query toolbar: text on the button next to Commit in manual commit mode that undoes the tab's open transaction; verb.

rollback_tooltip.location: Workbench → Query toolbar: tooltip on the Rollback button in manual commit mode, which rolls back (discards) the tab's open transaction.

copied.location: Workbench → Status bar: success message on macOS/Linux after a “Copy CLI command” button in a tool dialog (export, dump, restore, schedule) puts the equivalent sqlly-cli command on the clipboard.

copied_windows.value: CLI 명령을 복사했습니다 (POSIX 셸 구문 — Git Bash 또는 WSL에서 실행)
copied_windows.location: Workbench → Status bar: Windows variant of the copied-CLI-command message, warning that the copied line uses POSIX shell syntax and must be run from Git Bash or WSL.

auto_scroll_menu.location: Diagnostic Log panel → Header ⋮ menu: checkable item that keeps the log scrolled to the newest entry as new lines arrive.

clear_menu.location: Diagnostic Log panel → Header ⋮ menu: item that removes all entries currently shown in the diagnostic log; verb.

copy_menu.location: Diagnostic Log panel → Header ⋮ menu: item that copies the selected log text, or the whole log if nothing is selected, to the clipboard; verb.

entry_count.location: Diagnostic Log panel (bottom of the window, View → Toggle Log Console) → Header: panel title with the total number of log lines; {count} is that number.

error_count.location: Diagnostic Log panel → Header: red counter beside the title, shown only when the log contains errors; {count} is the number of error entries.

capabilities_section.location: View menu → IntelliSense Debug panel → Report body: heading of the first section, showing the JSON capabilities the language server would return to the initialize request; LSP protocol names, normally left untranslated.

clear_button.location: View menu → IntelliSense Debug panel → Header bar: clickable “Clear” text at the far right that empties the panel's report until the next refresh.

completion_count.location: View menu → IntelliSense Debug panel → Header bar: dim counter after the cursor offset; {count} is how many completion suggestions IntelliSense returned at the cursor in the last snapshot.

completion_section.location: View menu → IntelliSense Debug panel → Report body: heading of the section listing the completion items the server would return for the cursor position; LSP method name followed by a short description.

computing.location: View menu → IntelliSense Debug panel → Report body → Diagnostics section: lowercase placeholder shown while the background SQL validation for the diagnostics section is still running.

cursor_offset.location: View menu → IntelliSense Debug panel → Header bar: compact technical label after the panel title; {offset} is the cursor's character offset in the active editor. Keep very short.

diagnostics_section.location: View menu → IntelliSense Debug panel → Report body: heading of the last section, showing the SQL validation diagnostics the server would report; LSP method name, normally left untranslated.

empty_document.location: View menu → IntelliSense Debug panel → Report body → Diagnostics section: JSON-style placeholder (empty list plus a code comment) shown when the active editor has no text, so there is nothing to validate.

empty_snapshot.value: 아직 스냅샷이 없습니다 — 새로 고침을 누르세요.
empty_snapshot.location: View menu → IntelliSense Debug panel → Report body: empty-state message shown before any report exists or after Clear, telling the user to click Refresh in the header.

hover_section.location: View menu → IntelliSense Debug panel → Report body: heading of the section showing the hover information the server would return for the word under the cursor; LSP method name.

items_unit.location: View menu → IntelliSense Debug panel → Report body → Completion section: plural unit noun inserted into the truncation marker when the completion list is cut off (“truncated (240 items)”).

no_active_connection.location: View menu → IntelliSense Debug panel → Report body → Diagnostics section: JSON-style placeholder (empty list plus a code comment) shown when the editor has no active connection, so validation does nothing.

panel_title.location: View menu → IntelliSense Debug panel → Header bar: title at the left of the bottom debug panel that shows what the IntelliSense language server would return for the active editor.

position_section.location: View menu → IntelliSense Debug panel → Report body: heading of the section showing how the cursor maps to a language-server position as zero-based line and character numbers.

refresh_button.location: View menu → IntelliSense Debug panel → Header bar: clickable “Refresh” text beside Clear that rebuilds the report from the active editor's current text and cursor.

semantic_tokens_section.location: View menu → IntelliSense Debug panel → Report body: heading of the section showing the syntax-coloring tokens the server would return for the whole document; LSP method name.

serialization_error.location: View menu → IntelliSense Debug panel → Report body: text shown in place of a section's JSON when that section could not be converted to JSON; {error} is the technical error.

token_tuples_unit.location: View menu → IntelliSense Debug panel → Report body → Semantic tokens section: plural unit noun inserted into the truncation marker when the token list is cut off (“truncated (900 token tuples)”).

truncated_marker.location: View menu → IntelliSense Debug panel → Report body: marker appended on a new line after an ellipsis when a large section is cut at about 8 KB; {count} is the total number and {unit} is “items” or “token tuples”.

cancelled_message.location: Tool output dialog → Body: text shown instead of a tool's output when the user stopped the tool (for example a dump, transfer or analysis) before it completed.

copy_button.location: Tool output dialog → Footer: button that copies the full output text shown in the dialog to the clipboard.

open_query_button.location: Tool output dialog → Footer: primary button, shown only when the output is SQL, that opens the output text in a new query tab.

ai_review_required.value: 이 연결은 데이터 변경에 대한 AI 검토가 필요합니다. 실행하려면 파일을 쿼리 탭에서 여세요.
ai_review_required.location: File menu → Run SQL File dialog → Review step: red warning replacing the safety summary when the connection requires AI review of data changes and the file contains changes; Run is disabled.

back_button.location: File menu → Run SQL File dialog → Review step → Footer: button at the left that returns to the setup step to change the file or run options.

batch_size_invalid.location: File menu → Run SQL File dialog → Status bar: validation message shown when Scan or Run is attempted with a batch size outside the allowed range; {minimum} and {maximum} are the limits.

batch_size_label.location: File menu → Run SQL File dialog → Setup step: field label for the number box setting how many single-row INSERTs may be combined into one statement.

cancel_run_button.location: File menu → Run SQL File dialog → Progress step → Footer: button that cancels the script while it runs; disabled once the run has ended.

choose_button.location: File menu → Run SQL File dialog → Setup step → SQL file row: button beside the path box that opens the system file picker to select the script.

coalesce_label.location: File menu → Run SQL File dialog → Setup step: checkbox label; when on, consecutive single-row INSERT statements are merged into multi-row INSERTs for speed. Dimmed for SQL Server.

database_changed.location: File menu → Run SQL File dialog → Run summary in the Tool output dialog: line added below the counts when the script switched databases; {database} is the database the session ended on.

decision_retry.location: File menu → Run SQL File dialog → Run summary → Failures list: word shown in parentheses after a failed statement when the user chose to retry it.

decision_skip.location: File menu → Run SQL File dialog → Run summary → Failures list: word shown in parentheses after a failed statement when the user chose to skip just that statement.

decision_skip_all.location: File menu → Run SQL File dialog → Run summary → Failures list: words shown in parentheses after a failed statement when the user chose to skip it and all later failures.

decision_stop.location: File menu → Run SQL File dialog → Run summary → Failures list: word shown in parentheses after a failed statement when the run stopped at it, by the user's choice or the On error setting.

detailed_summary.value:
명령문: 총 {total}개, 완료 {done}개, 실패 {failed}개, 건너뜀 {skipped}개
영향 받은 행: {rows}개
소요 시간: {elapsed_ms} ms
detailed_summary.location: File menu → Run SQL File dialog → Run summary in the Tool output dialog: three-line report after a run with statement counts by result, total rows affected, and elapsed time in milliseconds.

dialog_title.location: File menu → Run SQL File dialog: title of the dialog that streams a SQL script file to the current connection, also used as the prompt of its file picker. Command name.

failure_detail.location: File menu → Run SQL File dialog → Run summary → Failures list: one indented line per failed statement; {ordinal} is the statement number, {line} its starting line, {message} the error, {decision} the choice made.

failure_line.location: File menu → Run SQL File dialog → Progress step: red line listed under the progress text for each statement that failed during the run; {line} is its starting line and {message} the database error.

failures_heading.location: File menu → Run SQL File dialog → Run summary in the Tool output dialog: heading on its own line, after a blank line, introducing the list of statements that failed.

file_label.location: File menu → Run SQL File dialog → Setup step: field label for the path box and Choose button that select the script file to run.

file_required.location: File menu → Run SQL File dialog → Status bar: validation message shown when Scan or Run is attempted with the SQL file path left empty.

messages_heading.location: File menu → Run SQL File dialog → Run summary in the Tool output dialog: heading on its own line, after a blank line, introducing informational messages the server printed during the run.

on_error_ask.location: File menu → Run SQL File dialog → Setup step → On error dropdown: default option that pauses at each failed statement and asks whether to retry, skip, skip all or stop.

on_error_continue.location: File menu → Run SQL File dialog → Setup step → On error dropdown: option that records a failed statement and continues with the next one without asking.

on_error_label.location: File menu → Run SQL File dialog → Setup step: field label for the dropdown choosing what happens when a statement in the script fails.

on_error_stop.location: File menu → Run SQL File dialog → Setup step → On error dropdown: option that ends the whole run at the first failed statement.

open_failed.location: File menu → Run SQL File dialog → Status bar: error shown when Run starts but the chosen script file cannot be opened for reading; {error} is the system error.

progress_status.location: File menu → Run SQL File dialog → Progress step: status line under the progress bar; {statement} is how many statements have been processed, {line} the current file line, {rows} rows affected so far.

retry_button.location: File menu → Run SQL File dialog → Progress step → Footer: button shown while a failed statement awaits a decision; runs that statement again.

review_counts.location: File menu → Run SQL File dialog → Review step: first line after scanning; {units} is how many statements the file contains and {bytes} its size in bytes.

review_safety.value: 명령문 {units}개, 데이터 변경 {mutating}개 — 명령문별 검토 없이 실행됩니다
review_safety.location: File menu → Run SQL File dialog → Review step: safety line under the counts; {units} is the statement count and {mutating} how many change data, warning there is no per-statement review.

run_button.location: File menu → Run SQL File dialog → Review step → Footer: primary button that starts executing the scanned file; disabled when a blocking warning is shown.

run_cancelled.location: File menu → Run SQL File dialog → Status bar and notification center: message after the user cancels a run; {done} of {total} is how many statements completed.

run_failed.location: File menu → Run SQL File dialog → Status bar: error shown when the run could not proceed at all, for example a lost connection; {error} is the technical error.

run_finished.value: 실행 완료 — 명령문 {done}/{total}개, 영향 받은 행 {rows}개, {elapsed_ms} ms 소요
run_finished.location: File menu → Run SQL File dialog → Status bar and notification center: message after a run completes; shows {done} of {total} statements, {rows} rows affected and {elapsed_ms} milliseconds taken.

run_stopped.location: File menu → Run SQL File dialog → Status bar and notification center: message when a run ends at a failed statement; {done} of {total} is how many statements completed.

scan_button.location: File menu → Run SQL File dialog → Setup step → Footer: primary button that reads the file, counts its statements and moves to the review step.

scan_failed.location: File menu → Run SQL File dialog → Status bar: error shown when scanning the chosen file stops unexpectedly before any statement count is produced.

scan_open_failed.location: File menu → Run SQL File dialog → Status bar: error shown when Scan is clicked but the chosen file cannot be opened for reading; {error} is the system error.

scanning_button.location: File menu → Run SQL File dialog → Setup step → Footer: label of the disabled Scan button while the file is being read and counted.

skip_all_button.location: File menu → Run SQL File dialog → Progress step → Footer: button shown while a failed statement awaits a decision; skips it and every later failure without asking.

skip_button.location: File menu → Run SQL File dialog → Progress step → Footer: button shown while a failed statement awaits a decision; skips only that statement and continues.

stop_button.location: File menu → Run SQL File dialog → Progress step → Footer: button shown while a failed statement awaits a decision; ends the whole run there.

transaction_go_blocked.value: GO 배치가 포함된 스크립트에는 단일 트랜잭션을 사용할 수 없습니다.
transaction_go_blocked.location: File menu → Run SQL File dialog → Review step: red warning on SQL Server when Single transaction is chosen but the script has GO batch separators; Run is disabled.

transaction_label.location: File menu → Run SQL File dialog → Setup step: field label for the dropdown choosing whether the script runs inside one database transaction.

review_definer_current_user.value: DEFINER 절 {count}개가 실행 전에 CURRENT_USER로 변경됩니다.
review_definer_current_user.location: Run SQL File dialog → Review page: notice that the DEFINER clauses found in the script will be changed to CURRENT_USER (a SQL keyword, untranslated) before each statement runs; {count} is how many.

review_definer_strip.location: Run SQL File dialog → Review page: notice that the DEFINER clauses found in the script will be removed before each statement runs; {count} is how many.

review_definer_keep.value: 스크립트에 DEFINER 계정이 {count}개 지정되어 있습니다. 이 계정이 이 서버에 없으면 해당 명령문이 실패합니다.
review_definer_keep.location: Run SQL File dialog → Review page: notice when the script names DEFINER accounts and the user chose to keep them; {count} is the number of DEFINER clauses found.

definer_current_user.location: Run SQL File dialog → Setup page → DEFINER dropdown: option that rewrites every DEFINER clause to CURRENT_USER (a SQL keyword, kept untranslated).

definer_strip.location: Run SQL File dialog → Setup page → DEFINER dropdown: option that removes every DEFINER clause so objects are owned by the account running the script.

definer_keep.location: Run SQL File dialog → Setup page → DEFINER dropdown: option that runs the DEFINER clauses exactly as written in the script.

definer_label.location: Run SQL File dialog → Setup page (MySQL/MariaDB connections only): label to the left of the dropdown choosing what to do with DEFINER account clauses in the script.

transaction_none.location: File menu → Run SQL File dialog → Setup step → Transaction dropdown: default option; each statement commits on its own with no wrapping transaction.

transaction_single.location: File menu → Run SQL File dialog → Setup step → Transaction dropdown: option that wraps the whole script in one transaction so it all commits or rolls back together.

buy.location: Unlock SQLLY dialog (Mac App Store edition) → Footer: primary button that opens Apple's purchase sheet for the lifetime unlock; disabled until the price has loaded.

restore.location: Unlock SQLLY dialog (Mac App Store edition) → Footer: button at the left that restores a previous purchase made with the same Apple Account.

item.location: Unlock SQLLY dialog (Mac App Store edition) → Benefits list: one line per benefit, a check mark followed by {benefit}, which is the translated benefit text.

no_reminders.location: Unlock SQLLY dialog (Mac App Store edition) → Benefits list: benefit line saying the unlock stops the periodic prompts asking free users to support SQLLY.

one_time_purchase.location: Unlock SQLLY dialog (Mac App Store edition) → Benefits list: benefit line stressing the unlock is paid once, not a recurring subscription.

unlimited_connections.location: Unlock SQLLY dialog (Mac App Store edition) → Benefits list: benefit line saying the unlock removes the free edition's limit on saved connections.

title.location: Unlock SQLLY dialog (Mac App Store edition) → Title bar: dialog title; the window is opened from the app menu, from upgrade links, or when a free-tier limit blocks an action.

app_store_edition_only.value: 앱 내 구매는 SQLLY의 Mac App Store 버전에서만 가능합니다.
app_store_edition_only.location: Unlock SQLLY dialog → Status line: reason inserted as {error} into the price, purchase, or restore failure message when this build has no App Store purchasing (not the Mac App Store edition).

product_load_failed.value: App Store에서 제품을 불러오는 데 실패했습니다.
product_load_failed.location: Unlock SQLLY dialog (Mac App Store edition) → Status line: reason inserted as {error} into the price-loading failure message when the App Store gives no reason of its own.

purchase_incomplete.location: Unlock SQLLY dialog (Mac App Store edition) → Status line: reason inserted as {error} into the purchase failure message when the App Store gives no reason of its own.

purchase_linked_to_other_account.value: 이 App Store 구매는 이미 다른 SQLLY 계정에 연결되어 있습니다. 이 Mac에서는 SQLLY가 계속 잠금 해제된 상태로 유지되며, 해당 계정으로 로그인하면 그곳에서도 잠금이 해제됩니다.
purchase_linked_to_other_account.location: Unlock SQLLY dialog (Mac App Store edition) → Warning line under the status: shown when this Mac's App Store purchase is already recorded on a different SQLLY account.

restore_failed.value: App Store에서 구매를 복원할 수 없습니다.
restore_failed.location: Unlock SQLLY dialog (Mac App Store edition) → Status line: reason inserted as {error} into the Restore Purchases failure message when the App Store gives no reason of its own.

fallback_title.location: Unlock SQLLY dialog (Mac App Store edition) → Product row: product name shown beside the price while the App Store listing is loading or could not be loaded.

cancelled.location: Unlock SQLLY dialog (Mac App Store edition) → Status line under the benefits: shown after the user dismisses Apple's purchase sheet without buying.

failed.location: Unlock SQLLY dialog (Mac App Store edition) → Status line under the benefits: shown when the App Store purchase fails; {error} is the error from Apple.

pending.value: 구매 승인을 기다리는 중입니다. 승인되면 SQLLY가 자동으로 잠금 해제됩니다.
pending.location: Unlock SQLLY dialog (Mac App Store edition) → Status line under the benefits: shown when the purchase needs approval (for example Ask to Buy); explains SQLLY unlocks itself once approved.

failed.location: Unlock SQLLY dialog (Mac App Store edition) → Status line under the benefits: shown when Restore Purchases fails; {error} is the error from Apple.

not_found.value: 이 Apple 계정에 대한 SQLLY 구매가 없습니다.
not_found.location: Unlock SQLLY dialog (Mac App Store edition) → Status line under the benefits: shown after Restore Purchases finds no earlier SQLLY purchase on the signed-in Apple Account.

loading_price.location: Unlock SQLLY dialog (Mac App Store edition) → Status line under the benefits: progress text shown while the localized price is fetched from the App Store.

price_failed.value: App Store에서 SQLLY 가격을 불러올 수 없습니다: {error}
price_failed.location: Unlock SQLLY dialog (Mac App Store edition) → Status line under the benefits: error shown when the price could not be loaded and Buy stays disabled; {error} is the App Store error.

purchasing.location: Unlock SQLLY dialog (Mac App Store edition) → Status line under the benefits: progress text shown while Apple's purchase sheet is open and the purchase is in progress.

restoring.location: Unlock SQLLY dialog (Mac App Store edition) → Status line under the benefits: progress text shown after Restore Purchases is clicked while the App Store is checked.

unlocked.value: SQLLY가 잠금 해제되었습니다. 후원해 주셔서 감사합니다!
unlocked.location: Unlock SQLLY dialog (Mac App Store edition) → Status line under the benefits: thank-you message shown once SQLLY is owned; the Buy and Restore buttons are hidden.

unlocked_short.location: Workbench → Status bar: one-word success message shown right after a purchase or restore unlocks the Mac App Store edition.

cleaning_up.location: Update Summary dialog → Footer: disabled primary button label shown while files from an earlier failed update attempt are removed before downloading again.

download_version.location: Update Summary dialog → Footer: primary button label when this copy cannot update itself; opens the download for the new version; {version} is its number.

downloading.location: Update Summary dialog → Footer: disabled primary button label during the in-app download; {progress} is a percentage or megabytes received.

install_version.location: Update Summary dialog → Footer: primary button label that downloads and installs the new version in the app; {version} is the new version number.

restart.location: Update Summary dialog → Footer: primary button label once the update is downloaded and ready; restarts SQLLY to finish installing.

try_again.location: Update Summary dialog → Footer: primary button label after an in-app install failed; starts the download and install again.

verifying.location: Update Summary dialog → Footer: disabled primary button label shown after the download while the update package is checked and unpacked.

automatic_install_note.value: 설치하면 새 버전이 다운로드되고, SQLLY가 재시작되어 마무리됩니다. 열려 있는 탭과 저장되지 않은 쿼리는 그대로 유지됩니다.
automatic_install_note.location: Update Summary dialog → Body: small print above the download link explaining how the in-app install works; shown when this copy can update itself.

available_title.location: Update Summary dialog → Body: bold heading at the top announcing the new release; {version} is the latest version number.

cancel_idle_download.location: Update Summary dialog → Footer: button label while waiting for idle to download a version this copy cannot self-install; clicking cancels the wait.

cancel_idle_install.location: Update Summary dialog → Footer: button label while waiting for the app to become idle before installing; clicking cancels the pending install.

cancel_install_button.location: Update Summary dialog → Footer: button shown only while the update is downloading or unpacking; stops that job and restores the usual buttons.

check_again_button.location: Update Summary dialog → Footer: button that checks the update server again right away for a newer release.

download_label.location: Update Summary dialog → Body: label with a colon placed before the link to the website's download page for every platform.

download_when_idle.location: Update Summary dialog → Footer: button label, when this copy cannot self-install, that downloads once current work ends; {work} lists running work, such as “2 queries”.

install_failed_with_download.value: 업데이트를 설치할 수 없습니다: {error} 대신 아래 링크에서 다운로드할 수 있습니다.
install_failed_with_download.location: Update Summary dialog → Body: red error under the release notes after the in-app install fails; {error} is the reason, followed by a pointer to the download link.

install_when_idle.location: Update Summary dialog → Footer: button label, while work is running, that installs once it all finishes; {work} lists running work, such as “1 query, 1 dump”.

installed_version.location: Update Summary dialog → Body: dim line under the heading stating the currently installed version; {version} is that version number.

manual_install_note.value: {reason} 새 버전을 다운로드하고 현재 설치를 수동으로 교체하세요.
manual_install_note.location: Update Summary dialog → Body: small print shown when this copy cannot update itself; {reason} is a full sentence explaining why, followed by this instruction.

restart_when_idle.location: Update Summary dialog → Footer: button label, once the update is ready but work is running, that restarts after it finishes; {work} lists the running work.

skip_button.location: Update Summary dialog → Footer: button that skips this version so SQLLY stops announcing it; later versions are still offered.

skipped_note.value: v{version} 버전을 건너뛰었습니다 — 다운로드하면 건너뛰기가 해제됩니다.
skipped_note.location: Update Summary dialog → Body: dim note shown when a version was previously skipped; {version} is that version; downloading clears the skip.

snooze_button.location: Update Summary dialog → Footer: button that closes the dialog and postpones the update reminder for a while.

startup_notice_toggle.location: Update Summary dialog → Footer: checkbox at the left; when on, this dialog opens at launch whenever an update is available.

title.location: Update Summary dialog → Title bar: title of the dialog listing what is new since the installed build, with buttons to install, skip or postpone the update.

waiting_for_idle.location: Update Summary dialog → Body: dim note under the version lines shown while an install-when-idle request is pending; points to the cancel button in the footer.

already_current.location: Update Summary dialog → Install error: install failure reason shown when, at download time, the latest published release turns out to be no newer than the running copy; also follows “Update failed:” in the status bar.

browser_current.location: Update Summary dialog → Manual-install small print: reason in the browser preview explaining it cannot install updates because the web version is always the latest; shown before the sentence telling the user to download and replace manually.

cancelled.location: Update Summary dialog → Install error: message reported when the user pressed Cancel while the in-app update was downloading or unpacking; the dialog returns to its idle buttons.

checksum_mismatch.value: 다운로드가 게시된 체크섬과 일치하지 않아 폐기되었습니다. 다시 시도하거나 sqlly.app에서 다운로드하세요.
checksum_mismatch.location: Update Summary dialog → Install error: install failure reason shown when the downloaded update's SHA-256 checksum does not match the one published for the release, so the file was deleted; also follows “Update failed:” in the status bar.

checksum_missing.value: 이 릴리스는 게시된 체크섬이 없어 SQLLY가 다운로드를 확인할 수 없습니다. 대신 sqlly.app에서 다운로드하세요.
checksum_missing.location: Update Summary dialog → Install error: install failure reason shown when the release on sqlly.app has no recorded checksum, so the in-app installer refuses it and points to the website download; also follows “Update failed:” in the status bar.

command_failed.location: Update Summary dialog → Install error: generic install failure when a system helper program (disk mount, copy, signature check, unpack) ran but exited with an error; {operation} is a short verb phrase such as “unpack the update”, {error} is the helper's error output.

command_spawn_failed.location: Update Summary dialog → Install error: generic install failure when a system helper program (disk mount, copy, signature check, unpack) could not even be launched; {operation} is a short verb phrase such as “open the disk image”, {error} is the system's launch error.

copy_new_version.location: In-app update → Failed step name (macOS): verb phrase in lowercase that fills {operation} in “Couldn't {operation}: {error}”; must read naturally after “Couldn't”/“No se pudo”; names the step that copies the new SQLLY.app out of the mounted disk image next to the installed app.

disk_image.value: SQLLY가 디스크 이미지에서 실행 중입니다. 먼저 응용 프로그램 폴더로 드래그하세요.
disk_image.location: Update Summary dialog → Manual-install small print: reason (macOS) the copy cannot update itself because SQLLY is being run straight from the mounted installer disk image; tells the user to drag it to Applications first.

disk_image_no_app.location: Update Summary dialog → Install error: install failure reason (macOS) shown when the downloaded and mounted disk image contains no .app bundle to copy; also follows “Update failed:” in the status bar.

disk_image_read_failed.location: Update Summary dialog → Install error: install failure reason (macOS) shown when the contents of the mounted update disk image cannot be listed; {error} is the file-system error text.

download_directory_failed.value: 업데이트 다운로드 폴더({path})를 생성할 수 없습니다: {error}
download_directory_failed.location: Update Summary dialog → Install error: install failure reason shown when the temporary folder for the update download cannot be created; {path} is the folder path, {error} is the file-system error.

download_http_failed.location: Update Summary dialog → Install error: install failure reason shown when sqlly.app answers the update download request with an HTTP error; {status} is the numeric HTTP status code, such as 404.

download_incomplete.location: Update Summary dialog → Install error: install failure reason shown when the update download ended with fewer bytes than the server announced; also follows “Update failed:” in the status bar.

download_interrupted.location: Update Summary dialog → Install error: install failure reason shown when the network connection dropped partway through downloading the update; also follows “Update failed:” in the status bar.

download_save_failed.location: Update Summary dialog → Install error: install failure reason shown when the downloaded update cannot be written or renamed on disk (for example a full disk); {error} is the file-system error.

download_server_unreachable.value: 업데이트를 다운로드하기 위해 sqlly.app에 연결할 수 없습니다.
download_server_unreachable.location: Update Summary dialog → Install error: install failure reason shown when SQLLY cannot connect to sqlly.app, either to look up the latest release or to fetch the file; also follows “Update failed:” in the status bar.
